m1-nature: Technical communication, definition 1?
The exchange of information that helps people interact with technology and solve complex problems.
Technical communication, definition 2?
The art and science of making complex technical information accessible, usable and relevant to a variety of audiences in a variety of settings.
Primary goal of technical writing?
Make complex information easy for the intended audience to understand and use.
Who writes technical documents?
Engineers and scientists traditionally, but also doctors, nurses, lawyers, farmers: any field with jargon.
Laplante's point about everyone?
Everyone is a technical writer occasionally: directions, recipes, complaint letters.
Do equations define technical writing?
No. A document can be step-by-step procedures with no equation.
Precision: the 1962 example?
NASA's Mariner 1 lost partly through a misplaced hyphen.
Intent of technical writing vs poetry, news, advertising?
No intent to evoke emotion: convey information concisely and correctly.
Harms from technical errors, per the slides?
Financial loss, property damage, environmental catastrophe, injury, death.
Which book on punctuation does the deck name?
Lynne Truss, Eats, Shoots and Leaves.
Ambiguity in bills of quantities triggers about what share of disputes?
About 34.2% of construction contract disputes.
m1-features: The eight characteristics of technical writing?
Precision; professional, not emotional, but persuasive; accuracy; clarity; completeness; diction; organization; visual effectiveness.
Precision in terms of other qualities?
Six skills of a technical writer?
Subject expertise, design, technical tools, writing and editing, conveying information, research and audience analysis.
Four safety labels shown in the manual slide?
m1-kinds: Three types of technical writing?
Consumer-directed, expert-to-expert, technical marketing.
Consumer-directed examples?
User manuals, employee handbooks, SOPs, help files, troubleshooting guides, legal disclaimers.
Expert-to-expert examples?
Scientific papers, medical case studies, annual business reports, legal case reviews.
Technical marketing examples?
Marketing case studies, white papers, brochures, press releases, business plans and proposals.
Purpose of technical marketing content?
Technical information in a digestible format that promotes a product or service.
Audience of a booklet that comes with a computer?
End users: first use, maintenance, warnings.
Purpose of internal or client documentation?
Inform others of the technical aspects of a product or its development; keep members updated for decisions.
Five kinds of technical communication in the textbook diagram?
Instructions, user guide, report, memo, procedures.
Four branches of the documentation tree?
Product and user, process, expert-to-expert, sales and marketing.
Parts of an SOP shown on the slide?
Title, department, date and ID, sign-off, purpose, definitions, procedure.
Columns of the SLA sample?
Service, description, SLA target, performance metric, measurement.
m1-taxonomy: The broadest form, serving practitioners in any discipline.
Scientific writing, technical reporting, business communications (and electronic media on the second slide).
A system that organises the information inside documents so users can find it.
Forms of a knowledge organisation system?
Controlled vocabulary, synonym ring, thesaurus, term tree, ontology.
Which orientation is a novice photographer's guide?
Which branch of professional is a progress report?
m1-scientific-reporting: Supervisors, subordinates, peers, customers, clients, government agencies.
Convey specific information in an archival way, stored for years.
Progress reports, feasibility studies, specifications, proposals, manuals, safety analysis reports.
Extra examples in the longer list?
Facilities descriptions, procedures, planning documents, environmental impact statements, bug reports.
The two things a scientific writer balances?
Books, journals, magazines, conferences, newsletters, websites and blogs.
Highest authority, slowest venue in the chart?
m1-business: Business communication is…
Correspondence written during the daily course of business activities.
Five examples on the theory slide?
Résumés, cover letters, transmittal letters, customer relations writing, administrative communications.
Two extra examples in the longer deck?
Human resources communications and trip reports.
How does business tone differ from a technical report's?
It often aims for a call to action; a technical report is neutral.
Does business writing still need precision?
Yes. Precision is still required.
Four blocks of the sample résumé?
Work experience, skills and competencies, achievements and certificates, interests.
The slide task for a biosketch?
Write one about yourself in 50 words or less.
Business plan sections (eight)?
Executive summary, product description, SWOT analysis, market research, organizational system, schedule, financial planning, appendix.
The most critical business plan section?
Financial planning.
m1-5cs-overview: Why does the textbook make its own 5 Cs?
There is no widely accepted quality standard for technical writing, only document templates such as IEEE 829-1998.
Where do the 5 Cs come from?
IEEE 830, the requirements engineering standard for System Requirements Specifications (retired 2011).
The eight IEEE 830 qualities?
Correct, unambiguous, complete, consistent, ranked for importance and/or stability, verifiable, modifiable, traceable.
Which three IEEE qualities are dropped?
Ranked, verifiable, traceable.
The 5 Cs?
Correct, Clear, Complete, Consistent, Changeable.
Which two words were swapped to get the Cs?
Unambiguous to clear and modifiable to changeable.
Precision in terms of the 5 Cs?
Clarity plus correctness.
Best way to establish the 5 Cs?
Peer review. Spell, grammar and writing-level tools help a little.
What is a System Requirements Specification?
A typical technical document giving a high-level description of the functions and features of a proposed system.
m1-5cs-qualities: Correct means…
Grammatically and technically correct information.
The textbook's incorrect weight sentence?
200 kilograms where 2000 was intended (technical error); an extra "shall" is the grammar error.
Why can't a spell checker find "200 kilometers" wrong?
No spelling error: it is a logic error. Tools cannot check technical correctness.
Clear means…
Each sentence, group of sentences or section has only one interpretation (unambiguous).
The textbook's example of unclear writing?
The car manual rule to reset the warning light: three consecutive error-free cold starts, a cold start needing eight hours since the last start-up.
Complete means…
No relevant or important information is missing, relative to the reader's needs.
Best technique to reduce incompleteness?
Have as many people as possible read it; log missing items for the next version.
Internal versus external consistency?
Internal: no part contradicts another part. External: agrees with all other applicable documents and standards.
Changeable means…
The structure readily yields to modification: numbered, convenient electronic format, compatible with processing and configuration tools.
Why is changeability important?
Content will change; ease of change reduces costs, helps schedules and communication.
m1-5cs-example: What kind of document is the 5 Cs example?
An excerpt from a systems specification for a smart home entertainment system, on recording TV shows.
Which C does the author find clearly failing?
Clear: many ambiguous phrases.
The author's test for clarity?
Ask "How do I test this?"
Why is "any show on television" unclear?
U.S. or worldwide? Pay-per-view? The scope is not stated.
Why is "X episodes" unclear?
It does not say what kind of number X is.
Verdict on Correct?
Fits common understanding, but needs analysis, focus groups and experts to be sure.
Verdict on Consistent?
No guarantee in natural language; only formal methods allow rigorous evaluation. Informal reading found nothing.
What does Changeable need here?
A change management tool tracking changes, sources and dates.
Why number the lines of an SRS?
To reference specific requirements later.
Best way to establish the Cs?
Peer review.
m1-references: Why must you choose references with judgment?
Your list says a lot about your familiarity with the subject.
How old is too old for fast-changing technology?
More than ten years.
What risk comes with too few references?
The authority of the publication will be challenged.
What is over-referencing?
Too many references, especially duplicative ones such as two similar works by the same author.
Why not rely on books?
They age quickly.
Why not rely on conference papers?
They are not fully vetted.
Why not rely on journal articles alone?
They are often too theoretical.
Why not rely on Web references?
They lack the vetting and cognitive authority of the other types.
Best make-up of a reference list?
A balance of types.

m1-email-review: What should a subject line show?
The purpose, and urgency or key points where they matter.
Josh email: what is wrong with the time-off line?

Josh email: what is wrong with the team members line?

John's email: the proper salutation?

Michael's email: the main tone fault?

What should an email end with?
A professional closing, next steps and the sender's full name.
What title does the deck give the slide 20 email?

Strong replacement for "Please advise"?

Strong replacement for "I was wondering if..."?

m1-case-study: How long is the case-study answer?
200 to 250 words.
What does the sample question ask?
To identify the communication barrier and explain the losses incurred.
What did the XYZ president's memo demand?
That all employees use the company's app, or seek employment elsewhere.
Barriers named in the sample answer?
Organisational (inappropriate medium) and interpersonal (implied emotional outburst).
Why is the memo an organisational barrier?
A formal, impersonal medium was used for a highly personal, debatable demand.
Why is it an interpersonal barrier?
The ultimatum reads as an emotional outburst, close to professional incompetence.
Internal losses in the sample?
Trust and morale, with possible effects on productivity and retention.
External losses in the sample?
Damaged public image and doubts about the app's viability, after the leak.
What is the question really assessing?
Critical analysis and applying theory systematically.
May you name other barriers?
Yes, if you justify them logically.
m2-concord-rules: The basic concord rule?
A singular subject needs a singular verb; a plural subject needs a plural verb.
Which person takes "walks" in the basic pattern?
The third person singular: he, she, it walks.
Blue Book test for a singular verb?
Would you use it with he / she (singular) or with they (plural)?
Blue Book: how do you find the subject?
Find the verb first, then ask who or what performed it.
One of the glasses (is/are) empty.
is. The subject is one, not glasses.
The bouquet of red roses (smells/smell) sweet.
smells. The subject is bouquet.
Subjects joined by "and" take...
A plural verb: Meenu and Meera are coming home.
Neither the shoes nor the bag (match/matches)...
matches: the verb agrees with the noun closest to it, bag.
Matt, as well as his dog, (is/are) expected.
is. "As well as" is ignored; the subject is Matt.
Words ignored when choosing the verb (Rule 5)?
as well as, along with, besides, not.
In "Here are the chocolates", where is the subject?
It follows the verb: chocolates.
62 years (is/are) the minimum age of retirement.
is: a period of time as a unit.
Blue Book: where does "I" go in either/or?
Second, with am: Neither she nor I am going.
m2-concord-special: Portion words in the Blue Book rule?
percent, fraction, part, majority, some, all, none, remainder: the noun after of decides.
Both are given on the slide: is here OR are here.
group, population, family; the Blue Book adds team, staff.
Mathematics (is/are) very difficult for some people.
is: plural in form, singular in meaning.
Blue Book: each, everyone, somebody: singular or plural?
He is one of the men who (does/do) the work.
were: wish, request or contrary to fact.
m2-cond-basics: Two parts of a conditional sentence?
The if clause (condition) and the main clause (result).
Does clause order change the meaning?
No. The order of the clauses does not change the meaning.
Zero conditional form?
if + present simple, ... present simple.
When is the zero conditional used?
When the result will always happen.
If you heat water to 100 degrees, it ___.
boils (zero conditional).
First conditional form?
if + present simple, ... will + verb.
When is the first conditional used?
Future situations we believe are real or possible.
Modals allowed in a first-conditional main clause?
shall, should, will, would, can, could, may, might.
Real, first, second, third: likelihood?
true / likely or possible / less likely or less possible / impossible.
Type I, II, III if clauses on slide 3?
If I study / If I studied / If I had studied.
m2-cond-unreal: Second conditional form?
if + past simple, ... would + verb.
Use of the second conditional?
To imagine impossible or unlikely present or future situations.
Third conditional form?
if + past perfect, ... would + have + past participle.
Use of the third conditional?
A past situation that didn't happen, and its imagined result.
If I won the lottery, I ___ a big house.
would buy (second conditional).
If she had studied, she ___ the exam.
would have passed (third conditional).
How is the second different from the first?
It is a lot more unlikely: twenty bedrooms is a dream; new shoes is likely.
Two uses of the second conditional?
Future things probably not going to be true, and impossible present situations.
If I had his number, I would call him. Why second?
I don't have his number now, so it's impossible to call him.
Modals in the second and third main clause (slide tables)?
should, would, might, could.
m2-cond-mixed: A blend of second and third; the if clause and main clause refer to different times.
If I had worked harder, I would be in a better job now. Time of each clause?
If I hadn't gotten the job in Tokyo, I wouldn't be with my current partner. Type?
It's really important. If it wasn't, I wouldn't have called you on your holiday. Type?

m2-voice-other: Modal passive pattern?

Passive of "You must learn this book."

Passive of "Students should learn all lessons."

Passive of "Shut the door."

Request, advice and order patterns?
You are requested / advised / ordered to...
What to do with please and kindly?
Remove them when converting.
me, her, them, us, him as the passive subject?
I, she, they, we, he.
by-phrase forms of I, she, they, we, he, who?

m2-tenses-forms: Why does tense matter in technical writing?
The tense itself carries real information, not just grammatical correctness.
Present simple: structure and time expressions?
Subject + V1; every day, usually, always.
Present continuous: structure and time expressions?
am/is/are + V-ing; now, at the moment.
Present perfect: structure and time expressions?
has/have + V3; already, yet, since, for.
Past simple: structure and time expressions?
V2; yesterday, last week, in 2022 (and ago, last year on the lookup table).
Past continuous: structure and time expressions?
was/were + V-ing; while, when.
Past perfect: structure and time expressions?
had + V3; before, after.
Future simple: structure and time expressions?
will + V1; tomorrow, next week.
Future perfect: structure and time expressions?
will have + V3; by, before.
Future perfect continuous?
will have been + V-ing; for, by the time.
"just", "already", "yet" call for...
The present perfect.
The five choosing questions end with...
Does the time expression indicate the tense?
m2-tenses-errors: Present continuous instead of present simple (every day indicates a routine).
Present perfect with a finished time (ago requires the past simple).
Incorrect sequence of tenses (reporting verb is in the past).
When is the past perfect right?
For an action completed before another past action.
Present reporting verb: what tense follows?
The tense usually shifts one tense back.
She said that the machine ___ faulty.

m2-pronouns: Which pronouns are subject pronouns?
I, you, he, she, it, we, they.
Which pronouns are object pronouns?
me, you, him, her, it, us, them.
Which pronoun follows a be verb in formal writing?
The subject pronoun: It is he. This is she speaking.
Tranh is as smart as she / her?
she: "as she is". Complete the sentence in your head.
When does it's take an apostrophe?
Only as a contraction of it is or it has. The possessive is its.
When are myself, himself and the other self words correct?
Only when they refer back to a word in the same sentence: I did it myself.
Who or whom?
he = who, him = whom. Test only the clause that holds the word.
Whoever or whomever?
him + he = whoever, him + him = whomever. If the whole clause is the subject, look inside it.
That or which?
that = essential, no commas. which = nonessential, in commas. who for people.
m2-modifiers: If the word answers how, it is an adverb: add -ly (fast never takes it).
sweet: describing, not actively sniffing. Active sense verb gets -ly.
Good or well after "did the job"?
well (adverb). Health also takes well: I do not feel well.
How do you compare two things? Three or more?
Two: -er / more (the older of the two). Three or more: -est / most.
more quickly. Never drop the -ly in the comparison.
Like or as if before a subject and verb?
as if (or as). Like takes only an object.
m2-effective-writing: Vague to concrete: "The weather was of an extreme nature on the west coast."
California had very cold weather last week.
Why does the Blue Book prefer active voice?
The subject performs the verb, and the responsible party can appear.
"There is a case of meningitis that was reported in the newspaper." Best fix?
The newspaper reported a case of meningitis.
Fix the double negative: "He is not unwilling to help."
Items in a list share the same grammatical form: spelling, grammar, and punctuation.
An opening action whose doer is not the next subject: "While walking across the street, the bus hit her."
What makes "After the show ended." a fragment?
It is a weak clause with no strong clause attached.
m2-confusing-words: When it means to cause: "He effected a commotion."
Lay or lie: "I want to ___ down for a nap."

Past tense of lie (recline) and lay (place)?

imply = hint without saying; infer = conclude from evidence.
assure = to promise or say with confidence; ensure = to make sure something will or will not happen; insure = to issue an insurance policy.

m2-transitions-use: Joining two strong clauses with only a comma instead of a conjunction, a semicolon, or a period.
Comma before and, but, or, for, nor?
Yes, between two strong clauses; it may be omitted if both clauses are short.
Comma after a starting weak clause?
Yes: If you are not sure about this, let me know now. No comma when the strong clause comes first.
However or therefore as an interrupter?
Commas on both sides: I would, therefore, like a response.
However or therefore introducing a complete sentence?
Preferably a semicolon before and a comma after: I have paid my dues; therefore, I expect...

m3-why-define: Two things that decide which kind of definition you write?
Your purpose and your audience.
What does a definition establish between writer and reader?
Common ground: everyone means the same thing by the term.
Why is precise definition a legal matter?
You or your organisation are legally responsible for the document.
A contract is a detailed, legally binding…

Challenger: management defined the risk based on…

The three types of technical definition?
Parenthetical, sentence, expanded.
Which type is the most formal?

m3-parenthetical: A parenthetical definition uses a synonym or phrase placed in…

"A brief is a legal document used in court." The fault?

A definition fixed for the whole document, so the term needn't be redefined.
Working definition of local fauna leaves out…
m3-expanded: Which definition type is a paragraph or longer?

Light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation.
Expansion method that says what the term does NOT mean?
Method that answers "How does it work?"
Comparing voice (1,000 Hz), TV and light frequencies illustrates…
Four rules for a visual in a definition?
Label it, introduce and explain it, place it near the text, credit borrowed visuals.
Method that answers "What is needed to make it work?"
Coherent light is light whose waves are…
m3-placing: When should an unfamiliar term be defined?
The first time the reader meets it.
In parentheses or in the margin beside the term.
Where do numerous sentence definitions go?
Where does an essential expanded definition go?
Where does a reference-only expanded definition go?
An alphabetical list of specialised terms and their definitions.
Laypersons get definitions without interrupting technical readers.
m3-inference: When we make inferences, we reach conclusions based on…
Inference is contrasted with learning by…
